{
 "cwd": "/workspace",
 "query": "FULL WEBSITE BRIEF / PRD – TutorLaunch Editorial Site (Astro Static Website Only)

Create a premium classic-style editorial website for a startup in the tutoring / private education space. The website is not an app, not a dashboard, not a marketplace with real accounts. It is a static marketing + editorial site that looks like a polished ProductHunt launch page mixed with a trusted education magazine. Use Astro as the main framework. It must run as a static site with local/mock/sample content only, no backend, no database, no login, no auth, no payments, no real API calls.

PROJECT NAME
TutorLaunch Journal
Tagline: “Smarter tutoring insights for ambitious learners and modern parents.”

GENERAL DIRECTION
I want the site to feel like a startup launch page but also like an editorial publication. Think ProductHunt layout energy: launch badge, upvote-style counters as decorative/static UI, featured cards, maker notes, clean sections, strong typography, community proof. But the visual style should be classic, trustworthy, academic, slightly premium. Not too futuristic. No neon cyberpunk. Use warm ivory background, navy text, soft gold accents, muted coral CTA color, subtle borders, serif headings + clean sans body.

IMPORTANT STATIC REQUIREMENTS
- Build with Astro.
- Static frontend only.
- No external services.
- No actual ProductHunt integration.
- No login / signup backend.
- No form submission backend. Forms can be decorative/static only.
- No live comments, no real voting, no account system.
- All article data, tutors, testimonials, categories, metrics, comments must be mock/static content in local arrays or markdown/content files.
- Site should be deployable as a static site.
- No 3D, no WebGL, no game mechanics, no canvas effects.
- Animations are required but simple frontend animations only: reveal on scroll, hover lift, ticker, tab switch, accordion, animated counters with static values, subtle page transitions.

PAGES / ROUTES
Please create a complex multi-page static editorial site:

1. Home Page /
Hero section:
- small launch badge: “Now featured: Summer Study Strategy 2026”
- headline: “The editorial home for better tutoring decisions.”
- subheadline explaining parents, students, and tutoring startups can discover guides, methods, study plans, and expert-backed tutoring ideas.
- CTA buttons: “Read the latest issue” and “Explore tutoring guides”
- right side should have a ProductHunt-inspired launch card with static upvote count, maker avatar row, category pills, rating stars, and mini comments preview.
- Add animated floating editorial snippets/cards around hero, but keep it tasteful.

Sections on home:
- Featured issue of the week with large editorial card.
- Trending tutoring guides grid, like ProductHunt product cards but for articles/guides.
- “Why families trust this resource” with 4 credibility cards.
- Static animated metrics: 120+ guides, 38 study templates, 14 subject tracks, 9 editor picks.
- Subject channels: Math, Science, English, Exam Prep, Languages, Study Skills, College Prep, Homeschool.
- Tutor startup spotlight section: static profiles of fictional tutoring startups.
- Parent questions accordion.
- Newsletter block (visual only, no backend) with input and button, show tiny note “Static demo form”.
- Footer with columns.

2. Articles / Guides Listing Page /guides
- Editorial listing page with filters as frontend-only UI. Filters can change visible cards using client JS or can be static tabs, but no backend.
- Categories: Parent Guide, Student Strategy, Tutor Operations, Exam Prep, Study Habits, Learning Science.
- Sort chips: Featured, Most Discussed, Newest, Quick Reads. These are static/interactivity only.
- Article cards should include title, excerpt, author, read time, category, static upvote count, static comment count.
- Include at least 12 mock articles.
- ProductHunt-like sidebar: “Today’s top picks”, “Editor’s badge”, “Upcoming topics”.

3. Article Detail Template /guides/[slug] or example static pages
Create at least 3 sample article detail pages using Astro content or static data.
Each article page should have:
- breadcrumb
- category pill
- big title
- subtitle / deck
- author card
- published date
- read time
- static launch-style voting widget on side or top
- table of contents
- rich editorial content sections with headings, quote block, checklist, comparison table, callout note, related guides.
- static comments section inspired by ProductHunt discussions, with mock comments only.
- “Was this guide useful?” decorative vote buttons, no persistence needed.

Sample article titles:
- “How to Choose a Tutor Without Overpaying in 2026”
- “The 45-Minute Tutoring Session Framework That Actually Works”
- “Parent Checklist: Before Your Child Starts Exam Prep”

4. Subject Channel Page /subjects
- Grid of subject tracks.
- Each track has classic card style: icon, summary, recommended age range, top guides, static popularity score.
- Add comparison strip: “Best for weekly support / Best for exam sprint / Best for confidence building”.
- Include animated hover effects.

5. Startup Spotlight Page /spotlight
This is an editorial showcase of fictional tutoring startups, not real integrations.
- ProductHunt-inspired layout with static launch cards.
- Each card: startup name, one-line pitch, topic, founder quote, launch rank, static upvotes, static comments, tags.
- Include 8 fictional startups such as: LessonNest, StudyHarbor, BrightSteps Tutoring, MentorMint, ExamCamp, FocusFox Learning, ScholarBridge, HomeworkAtlas.
- Include a “Maker note” section, all mock.

6. About Page /about
- Mission: make tutoring decisions clearer.
- Editorial principles: clarity, evidence, affordability, student confidence, parent-friendly language.
- Team cards with fictional editors and education researchers.
- Timeline of the publication.
- Press-style quote strip.

7. Static Style Guide /style-guide
I want a page showing the design system: colors, typography, buttons, cards, badges, article blocks, ProductHunt-style launch card components, accordions, newsletter module.

DESIGN STYLE
Classic startup editorial, not generic template.
- Background: warm ivory / parchment (#F8F3E8 or similar)
- Primary text: deep navy (#172033)
- Accent: antique gold (#C99A3D)
- CTA: refined coral / clay (#D85C4A)
- Cards: off-white with thin navy/gold borders
- Typography: elegant serif for headings, modern sans for body. Use system fonts or local-safe Google-font-like choices but don’t require external fetch if avoidable.
- Lots of whitespace, editorial grid, magazine-like rhythm.
- ProductHunt reference: upvote badges, launch cards, maker avatar stack, comment count pills, ranking chips, “featured today” sidebar. But make it education/tutoring themed.

ANIMATION / INTERACTION REQUIREMENTS
- Smooth reveal-on-scroll for sections.
- Hover animations on cards: lift, shadow, small border color change.
- Animated counter effect for static metrics.
- Accordion on FAQ.
- Tabs or chips on guides listing.
- Sticky mini table of contents on article pages for desktop.
- Sticky top nav with subtle blur.
- Optional marquee/ticker of article categories, but keep classic and not flashy.
- Button micro-interactions.
- Respect prefers-reduced-motion.

NAVIGATION
Top nav:
- Home
- Guides
- Subjects
- Spotlight
- About
- Style Guide
CTA button: “Browse Guides”
Mobile nav should collapse nicely.

CONTENT REQUIREMENTS
Please write realistic polished copy, not lorem ipsum. The tone should be confident, parent-friendly, startup editorial, a little ProductHunt-ish.
Use mock data for all articles, authors, startups, comments, metrics, etc.
Include at least:
- 12 guide cards
- 8 subject tracks
- 8 startup spotlight cards
- 6 testimonials or reader quotes
- 3 full article pages
- 5 FAQ accordion items
- 4 fictional team members

COMPONENTS TO BUILD
- Header / Navbar
- Footer
- Hero
- LaunchCard
- UpvoteBadge (static)
- ArticleCard
- FeaturedArticle
- SubjectCard
- StartupCard
- TestimonialCard
- FAQAccordion
- NewsletterBlock
- MetricCounter
- Badge / Pill
- TableOfContents
- CommentCard
- AuthorCard
- DesignTokenPreview for style guide

RESPONSIVE
Must look excellent on desktop, tablet, and mobile.
- Desktop: editorial multi-column layout.
- Tablet: 2 column cards.
- Mobile: stacked cards, readable article pages, sticky elements disabled if needed.
No horizontal overflow.

ACCESSIBILITY
- Semantic HTML.
- Good contrast.
- Keyboard-friendly buttons/links.
- Alt text for any images/placeholders.
- Focus styles.
- Reduced motion support.

ASSETS
Use CSS shapes, gradients, initials avatars, simple inline SVG icons, or placeholder blocks. Do not depend on remote image search. If images are needed, use local placeholder gradients/illustrations.

DELIVERABLE EXPECTATION
Create the Astro project structure and implement the complete static website. The final result should feel like a real startup editorial publication ready for a ProductHunt-style launch, but everything is static and self-contained.",

 },

  "The editorial home for better tutoring decisions.",

  "Explore tutoring guides",
  "Why families trust this resource",

 ]

"""Grade a Webdev task as the explorer does (verl recipes/design webdev-eval): render, shrink, judge.

No index.html in dist/ scores 0. A render that fails, or a judge that never answers, writes no reward (not scored):
neither says anything about the page."""
import base64
import io
import json
import os
import random
import subprocess
import sys
import time
import urllib.request
from pathlib import Path

sys.path.insert(0, "/tests")
os.environ["WEBDEV_GRADE_HTTP"] = "1"   # serve over loopback http so React/Vue/ES-module sites actually run
from webdev.eval_rubric import build_prompt  # noqa: E402
from webdev.shot import _build_shot_cmd, _parse_render_env, _parse_shot_b64  # noqa: E402
from webdev.verdict import parse_verdict  # noqa: E402

cfg = json.loads(Path("/tests/grade.json").read_text())
V = Path("/logs/verifier")
V.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
dist = Path(cfg["cwd"]) / "dist"


def done(reward: float | None, why: str, **extra) -> None:
    (V / "result.json").write_text(json.dumps({"reward": reward, "summary": why, **extra}, indent=1))
    print(why)
    if reward is None:
        print("not scored", file=sys.stderr)
        sys.exit(1)
    (V / "reward.txt").write_text(f"{reward}\n")
    sys.exit(0)


files = sorted(str(p.relative_to(dist)) for p in dist.rglob("*") if p.is_file())[:200] if dist.is_dir() else []
if "index.html" not in files:
    done(0.0, "The agent delivered nothing to dist/." if not files else "dist/ has no index.html, so there is no page to open.",
         delivered=files)
res = subprocess.run(["sh", "-c", _build_shot_cmd(f"file://{dist}/index.html")], capture_output=True, text=True,
                     timeout=150)   # SHOT_TIMEOUT_S
shot = {"output": (res.stdout or "") + "\n" + (res.stderr or "")}
shot_b64, console_errors = _parse_shot_b64(shot)
render_env = _parse_render_env(shot)
if render_env.get("proxy_failed") or not shot_b64:
    print(shot["output"][-2000:], file=sys.stderr)
    done(None, "external assets were unreachable on every route" if render_env.get("proxy_failed")
         else "the screenshot produced no image")
jpg = base64.b64decode(shot_b64)
try:   # eval_mode._shrink: the judge refuses shots over 20 MP; proportional, quality 75
    from PIL import Image
    Image.MAX_IMAGE_PIXELS = None
    im = Image.open(io.BytesIO(jpg))
    size = im.size
    if im.width * im.height > 20e6:
        k = (20e6 / (im.width * im.height)) ** 0.5
        im = im.convert("RGB").resize((max(1, int(im.width * k)), max(1, int(im.height * k))), Image.LANCZOS)
        b = io.BytesIO(); im.save(b, "JPEG", quality=75); jpg = b.getvalue(); size = im.size
except ImportError:
    size = None
(V / "screenshot.jpg").write_bytes(jpg)
# webdev-structural-gate@1: necessary conditions, not a replacement judge.
_gate_layout = {}
for _line in (shot["output"] or "").splitlines():
    if _line.startswith("LAYOUT:"):
        try:
            _gate_layout = json.loads(_line[len("LAYOUT:"):])
        except (ValueError, TypeError):
            pass
        break
if (not isinstance(_gate_layout, dict) or _gate_layout.get("error")
        or not isinstance(_gate_layout.get("text"), str)
        or not isinstance(_gate_layout.get("scroll_w"), (int, float))
        or not isinstance(_gate_layout.get("client_w"), (int, float))
        or _gate_layout["client_w"] <= 0):
    done(None, "Structural measurements unavailable; not scored.")
_gate_text = " ".join(_gate_layout["text"].split())
_gate_kw = cfg.get("gate_keywords") or []
_gate_fails = []
if not _gate_text:
    _gate_fails.append("blank rendered DOM")
if _gate_kw and not any(_kw.casefold() in _gate_text.casefold() for _kw in _gate_kw):
    _gate_fails.append("no brief-keyword DOM presence")
if _gate_layout["scroll_w"] > _gate_layout["client_w"] + 1:
    _gate_fails.append("horizontal overflow")
_gate_report = {"passed": not _gate_fails, "failed": _gate_fails,
                "dom_chars": len(_gate_text), "keywords": _gate_kw,
                "layout": _gate_layout}
(V / "structural_gates.json").write_text(json.dumps(_gate_report, indent=1))
if _gate_fails:
    done(0.0, "Structural gates failed: " + "; ".join(_gate_fails),
         structural_gates=_gate_fails)
content = [{"type": "image_url", "image_url": {"url": "data:image/jpeg;base64," + base64.b64encode(jpg).decode()}},
           {"type": "text", "text": build_prompt().format(query=cfg["query"][:1500])}]   # QUERY_CAP
url = os.environ.get("WEBDEV_JUDGE_URL", "https://router.huggingface.co/v1").rstrip("/") + "/chat/completions"
_judge_pin = cfg["judge"]
if os.environ.get("WEBDEV_JUDGE_REVISION") != _judge_pin["model_sha"]:
    done(None, "Judge deployment revision is unbound; not scored.")
(V / "judge_config.json").write_text(json.dumps(_judge_pin, indent=1))
body = json.dumps({"model": cfg["judge"]["request_model"], "temperature": 0, "max_tokens": 1024,  # webdev-temp0-pin@1
                   "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": content}]}).encode()
verdict, last = None, ""
for attempt in range(4):   # JUDGE_RETRIES, with eval_mode's backoff
    if attempt:
        time.sleep(min(60.0, 3.0 * (3 ** (attempt - 1))) * (0.5 + random.random()))
    try:
        req = urllib.request.Request(url, data=body, method="POST", headers={
            "Content-Type": "application/json", "Authorization": f"Bearer {os.environ.get('WEBDEV_JUDGE_KEY', '')}"})
        with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=180) as r:   # JUDGE_TIMEOUT_S
            _judge_reply = json.loads(r.read())
            if _judge_reply.get("model_revision") != _judge_pin["model_sha"]:
                done(None, "Judge response revision differs from the task pin; not scored.")
            msg = _judge_reply["choices"][0]["message"]
        v = parse_verdict(msg.get("content") or msg.get("reasoning_content") or "")
        if "_failed" not in v:
            verdict = v
            break
        last = v["_failed"]
    except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001
        last = f"{type(e).__name__}: {e}"[:200]
if not verdict:
    done(None, f"judge unavailable: {last}")
done(verdict["score"], verdict.get("reason", ""), dims=verdict["dims"], visual=verdict["visual"], screenshot_size=size,
     console_errors=console_errors[:1500] if console_errors not in ("", "[]") else "")

rationale: Gate trivial, off-brief and overflowing pages to a scored 0 before the vision call, cutting judge spend and the blank-page lottery. Passing pages reach the judge unchanged.

gate_keywords: The editorial home for better tutoring decisions.
